evals.prompt: I need to interview candidates for a senior customer support lead next week. Build me the interview.
evals.expected_output: 4-6 role-derived competencies, two behavioral questions per competency with pre-written probes, a BARS scorecard with concrete 1/3/5 anchors, one work-sample element, and calibration instructions for multiple interviewers.
expectations: Competencies are derived from the role's failure modes, not a generic list
Every question is behavioral (past-tense) with at least 3 follow-up probes
The scorecard has behaviorally anchored descriptions for low, middle, and high ratings
Independent scoring before group discussion is specified

evals.prompt: Give me a mock interview for a product manager role. Be realistic, don't go easy on me.
evals.expected_output: A realistic structured mock: one question at a time, STAR extraction with probing for missing quadrants, verification probes on vague answers, followed by strengths-gaps-rewrites feedback quoting the candidate's actual answers.
expectations: Questions are asked one at a time with follow-up probes on the actual answers
Vague or inflated answers receive verification probes for numbers, names, or failure detail
Feedback quotes the candidate's own words and provides improved rewrites
A story-bank recommendation mapped to competencies is included

evals.prompt: Write a user research script to find out if freelancers would pay for my invoicing app idea.
evals.expected_output: A script that asks about specific past invoicing behavior and spending, avoids all 'would you use/pay' hypotheticals, and follows a funnel from broad workflow questions to specific verification.
expectations: No question asks the participant to predict future behavior or hypothetical willingness to pay
Questions target specific past instances, such as the last time they invoiced a client
Questions about money target actual past spending on solving the problem
The script includes a closing question inviting what was not asked
